items.item_text: Demonstrated experience with managing calendars, coordinating meetings, and travel coordination. Skill in working as part of a team composed of faculty, staff and administrators.

The Administrative Assistant III will provide overall administrative to the Department of Medicine Administrative Office. General duties include: prepare correspondence, manage calendars, coordinate meetings, recruitment, scheduling interviews, and purchasing/travel coordination. Responsible for meeting minutes, monitoring and editing content for distribution. Generate and review reports as needed, using University financial systems and internal databases. Use Bruin Buy+ and Concur for purchasing and reimbursement requests, and preparing various other University accounting forms. Support for yearly events and special projects as assigned.
Demonstrated skill with procurement process: communicating with vendors, obtain price quotes, prepare purchase orders, collecting invoices, track deliveries and reconcile packing slips.
Working knowledge of UCLA’s Concur/BruinBuy system and Travel Express system.
Demonstrated ability to take detailed minutes at important meetings for the senior leadership of the Department.
Mathematical skills for the preparation of calculations and forecasts and to identify and resolve financial problems.
Skill in writing concise, logical and grammatically correct correspondence.
Skill in working as part of a team composed of faculty, staff and administrators.
Interpersonal skills to communicate diplomatically and effectively with all levels of faculty, staff and non-University entities, Ability to use judgment when dealing with confidential information.

Skill in performing a variety of tasks independently with minimal direction in a timely matter under conditions of fluctuating workloads, competing requirements, and changing deadlines and priorities.
Demonstrated ability to operate a computer with a Windows environment utilizing MS Office to perform word-processing, spreadsheet analysis, and database programming and management.

Reading skills to comprehend University policies and procedures, Skill in organizing and prioritizing workload in order to meet deadlines in light of changing and/or heavy workload and competing requirements.
Skill in organizing and maintaining up to date, accurate bookkeeping records on-line and maintaining alpha-numeric files.
Skill in performing with frequent interruptions and/or distractions.
